headline: Allegro returns to profit as demand surges across markets
summary_short: Allegro MicroSystems posted revenue of $259.2M, up 27.5% y/y, swinging to $15.9M of net income and $0.09 basic EPS from a year-ago loss, as gross margin expanded to 48.5% from 44.9%.
summary_long: Revenue rose 27.5% y/y to $259.2M on Automotive growth (safety/comfort, ADAS, xEV) and Industrial growth (data-center, industrial-transport demand), with Taiwan sales up 219% on data-center orders. Gross margin expanded to 48.5% from 44.9% on higher volume, operating leverage and pricing actions. R&D fell to 21.3% of sales from 22.9% and SG&A fell to 17.3% from 23.4%, both aided by revenue growth and lower outside-services spend. Operating income swung to $25.5M from a $2.7M loss, and net income reached $15.9M ($0.09 basic EPS) versus a $13.2M loss a year ago, helped by lower interest expense from term-loan paydowns. Operating cash flow fell to $22.0M from $61.6M on working-capital timing; cash ended at $162.0M. No forward guidance was disclosed.

drivers.explanation: Automotive grew on safety/comfort/ADAS and xEV demand; Industrial and Other grew on data-center and industrial-transport demand; Taiwan sales rose 219% on data-center orders.
Rose on higher production volume supporting higher product sales; as a share of sales it fell to 51.5% from 55.1% on the revenue increase.
Gross margin expanded to 48.5% from 44.9% on higher net sales, operating leverage, pricing actions and a favorable product mix shift.
Opex grew slower than revenue: R&D fell to 21.3% of sales from 22.9%, and SG&A fell to 17.3% from 23.4% on lower outside-services spend, partly offset by higher personnel costs.
Tracks the operating-income swing plus lower interest expense from term-loan paydowns and January 2026 refinancing, partly offset by a $3.6M equity-method loss on the Polar Semiconductor investment.
Follows pretax income's swing to profit; the effective tax rate also improved to 8.6% from (31.7)% on higher pretax income, an FDDEI deduction and R&D credit benefits.
Tracks the net-income swing to profit; basic share count grew only modestly, so nearly all of the net-income gain flowed through to per-share earnings.
Tracks the net-income swing to profit; diluted share count rose only 1.7% y/y, so nearly all of the net-income gain reached diluted EPS.

Fell versus a year ago that had benefited from a large one-time decrease in prepaid expenses and other assets and lower payments to a related party; this quarter saw higher advance payments to the related party instead.
Capex was $8.0M versus $10.6M a year ago, both consisting solely of property, plant and equipment purchases; the release does not explain the size of the year-over-year decline.
Cash grew y/y as cumulative profitability and operating cash generation more than offset term-loan paydowns and capex versus a year ago; no buybacks or dividends were disclosed.
Declined on scheduled term-loan repayments and the January 2026 refinancing, which also lowered interest expense y/y.
Grew on retained-earnings additions from net income and stock-based compensation, partly offset by tax payments on net-settled equity awards; no buybacks were disclosed.
Rose modestly on equity-award vesting and stock-based compensation issuance in the ordinary course; no buyback was disclosed to offset it.

Management attributes the quarter to Automotive (ADAS, xEV, safety/comfort) and Industrial (data-center, industrial-transport) demand growth across geographies; the filing states no numeric forward guidance.
